If you only remember one thing: A I is now an election issue, and the chip war is shaping who builds what.

Number one. Nvidia's C E O and the spy story. From your Rundown newsletter. Nvidia's board ordered an independent review after reports that Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Huang admitted an affair in a letter to staff. The board says it sees no reason to believe secrets were compromised, and he stays C E O. He has until November eleventh to answer a House Republican request for a private briefing. Why it matters: Nvidia touches almost every part of the A I industry, so its leadership and China ties matter far beyond one boardroom.

Number two. A I and data centers swung the midterms. From your Tech Policy Press newsletter. Democrats won big on Tuesday. An N B C exit poll found fifty six percent of voters called A I and data centers a major factor. A C B S poll found most voters oppose a data center in their community. Expect hearings in twenty twenty seven, with the Doge data grab and Big Tech power on the list. Why it matters: A I regulation just became a mainstream political issue.

Number three. Anthropic's Claude dreams. From your Rundown. Anthropic shared how Claude agents use downtime to check and reorganize their memory notes against logs of past work. Newer models are better at deciding what to save. Why it matters: agents that remember the job and improve over time are the next step.

Number four. China's A I and chips squeeze. From your Recode China A I digest. Apple is testing Alibaba's Qwen inside Apple Intelligence in China, with a December rollout planned. Tencent released Hy four, with vision and computer use. Oracle reportedly dropped a seven billion dollar chip access deal with Tencent after U S concerns. And DeepSeek plans to train its next model on Huawei Ascend chips. Why it matters: export controls are pushing China toward its own chips and its own distribution.

Number five. Good news. Humanitarian groups, including the International Rescue Committee, are urging tech companies to put A I to work for displaced people. Also in your Reads: The Rundown's roundtable on everyday A I uses, like a Claude scheduled task that watches error charts and only alerts the team when something is really wrong.

The thread today: power, politics and chips are now one story. Have a great Monday.
